subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp scenarios - SagePath
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@sagepath.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp scenarios - SagePath

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the time last week — good conversation on expected peak loads and model mix. Attached is a concise set of reservation options tuned to the profile you shared (chat + embeddings heavy, spiky inference traffic during batch scoring windows). I kept the options focused so procurement has clear tradeoffs.

Summary (high level):

- Option A — Starter Lane
  - Minimum committed: 10 A100-equivalent GPUs
  - Typical throughput target: ~120k tokens/min sustained
  - Ramp: immediate activation, 1–2 week warmup to reach baseline; burst to 25 GPUs for scheduled scoring windows
  - Pricing: monthly committed fee + lower per-token overage rate for bursts

- Option B — Growth Lane (recommended mid-market path)
  - Minimum committed: 25 A100-equivalent GPUs
  - Typical throughput target: ~300k tokens/min sustained
  - Ramp: staged activation over 6 weeks (10 -> 18 -> 25) with 2x warm-start credit in week 1
  - Includes 4 hours/week of priority support onboarding + one deployment canary run

- Option C — Anchor Lane (enterprise ramp)
  - Minimum committed: 50 A100-equivalent GPUs
  - Typical throughput target: ~650k tokens/min sustained with geo-bursting option
  - Ramp: 12-week phased activation with pre-warm windows and regional pinning (US-west primary, US-east secondary)
  - Includes SLA uplift, dedicated capacity lane, and quarterly model tuning consults

Key callouts and optional controls:
- Warmup credits: we can front-load warm-start compute credits to reduce cold-start token cost during your first 4 weeks.
- Canary strategy: recommended small-scale canary (2 GPUs) before each phase to validate throughput and KV-cache behavior.
- Geo-fallback: we can define failover routing to a lower-cost variant in a different region (adds latency but preserves availability).
- Decommit guardrails: staged stepdown windows to avoid abrupt loss of capacity mid-quarter.

Attachments: SagePath_Reserve_Options_v3.pdf (breakdown by month, burn forecast, and activation calendar).

Next step: if Growth Lane looks closest to what you had in mind, I can send a one-page mutual action plan and a clean DocuSign-ready quote for procurement. If Procurement wants a different cadence for minimums, we can sketch a staggered tranche (e.g., 8/8/9/0 in month-steps) instead of the 10-18-25 progression.

Open to a 30-minute follow-up with procurement to walk the numbers.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.inference
[Attachment: SagePath_Reserve_Options_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 540KB)]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@sagepath.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, SagePath Procurement <procurement@sagepath.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and ramp scenarios - SagePath

Thanks Avery — this is helpful and clear. A few quick clarifications from my side before procurement kicks off: 

1) SLA and credits: for the Growth Lane do you offer target p99 latency SLAs? If we hit an outage window during ramp, what is the compensation mechanism?
2) Regional pinning: can reserved capacity be split across us-west and us-east from day one, or do we need to activate a single region then add another?
3) Burst behavior: if our scheduled scoring spikes exceed the burst cap, will requests queue or fail? We prefer graceful queuing policies.

Procurement (cc'd) — we will likely move forward with Growth if the SLA language and regional flexibility look good. I attached the MATP (minimal acceptance & procurement table) we use internally — please populate any required fields you need for legal and I.T. security to review.

If useful, can we do a procurement kickoff this Friday at 10 PT?

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, SagePath
lena.ortiz@sagepath.ai
[Attachment: SagePath_MATP.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 38KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity options and ramp scenarios - internal notes

Avery / Priyom — quick internal note before we reply: 

- Recommend we position Growth Lane as the default with a negotiated SLA p99 target of 1200 ms for chat workloads; offer service credits on a graduated scale (5% credit for partial-month impacts, 15% for sustained breach > 24 hours). That’s defensible and matches other mid-market comps.
- For region split ask: offer initial activation in US-west with an optional warm standby in US-east that can be turned to active within 72 hours (describe as "hot-warm"). This avoids double-reserving full capacity but gives a reasonable RTO.
- Burst handling: propose queue-first policy with autoscale thresholds: queue for up to 90 seconds, then overflow to best-effort burst if queue exceeds threshold. Spell that out in the MAP.
- For DocuSign: attach a one-page quote and the MAP; include a 30-day early termination (ET) buffer only if they commit to >12 months.

I'll draft the MAP language and the quote skeleton today — Priyom can you add the activation cadence numbers and warm-start credits to the spreadsheet Lena provided?

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@sagepath.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options and ramp scenarios - SagePath

Avery, Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. Procurement reviewed the MATP and we discussed internally. We want to proceed with the Growth Lane with two small adjustments: 

- Ramp cadence tweak: start 12 GPUs month 1, add 7 GPUs month 2, reach 25 by month 3 (our scoring windows are front-loaded in month 3).
- Regional requirement: please include a warm-standby in US-east with documented activation steps and a 72-hour SLA to flip. We understand the standby has different economics.

Procurement would like the one-page MAP + DocuSign quote and the SLA language spelled out (p99 target and credit formula). We are targeting a signature by Nov 30.

I attached the filled MATP with our account code and preferred billing contact. Please send the MAP and quote and we will route to legal.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, SagePath
[Attachment: SagePath_MATP.xlsx (updated)]
